description: Held-out, human-labeled claim-to-evidence benchmark for evaluating the HackathonOS verification system. Single-annotator gold labels.

questions.question_text: What is the directory structure of HackathonOS?
questions.answer_text: HackathonOS has 11 top-level directories: adapters, audits, commands, core, docs, rules, templates, tests, workflows, plus hidden directories .claude, .kilo, and .opencode.

questions.question_text: What programming language and configuration format does HackathonOS use?
questions.answer_text: HackathonOS is written in Python and uses JSON configuration files (manifest.json, settings.json, hackathon.json) plus dotenv environment files.

questions.question_text: What are the autonomous operation limits in HackathonOS?
questions.answer_text: Maximum 5 auto iterations, maximum 10 auto fixes, and human approval is required for autonomous operations.
Verification is enabled by default. ENABLE_AUTO_VERIFY=true in .env.example and verification.enabled=true in settings.json.

questions.question_text: What is the lifecycle phase structure of HackathonOS?
questions.answer_text: HackathonOS has exactly 20 lifecycle phases, with Phase 11 being Testing + Security.
HackathonOS implements 29 commands across 7 groups (CORE, CONFIGURATION, INTELLIGENCE, ENGINEERING, PRODUCT QUALITY, FINALIZATION, EMERGENCY) with master command /hackathonos.

questions.question_text: How does HackathonOS handle secrets and security?
questions.answer_text: Secrets are protected via .gitignore patterns for .env, .env.*, credentials, keys, pem files, and service-account.json. AI API keys are never stored in plain text.

questions.question_text: What is the current state of the HackathonOS repository?
questions.answer_text: The repository is on branch main with no .hackathon/ directory, no README.md at root, and no deployed application.
HackathonOS supports three host adapters: Claude Code, OpenCode, and Kilo Code.

questions.question_text: What evidence types does HackathonOS classify?
questions.answer_text: HackathonOS classifies evidence as FACT, INFERENCE, ASSUMPTION, or UNKNOWN.

reference_corpus.title: Configuration manager source
reference_corpus.text: HackathonOS configuration manager is written in Python. It parses dotenv files, loads JSON configuration, validates URLs, timezones, deadlines, and scans for secrets. Boolean keys include ENABLE_WEB_RESEARCH, ENABLE_AUTO_VERIFY, ENABLE_RED_TEAM, ENABLE_VIDEO_ASSIST, REQUIRE_HUMAN_APPROVAL.

Capability preferences: ENABLE_WEB_RESEARCH=true, ENABLE_AUTO_VERIFY=true, ENABLE_RED_TEAM=true, ENABLE_VIDEO_ASSIST=true. Autonomous safety limits: MAX_AUTO_ITERATIONS=5, MAX_AUTO_FIXES=10, REQUIRE_HUMAN_APPROVAL=true.

reference_corpus.title: Settings template
reference_corpus.text: agent_platform: UNKNOWN, ai_provider: UNKNOWN, ai_model: UNKNOWN, verification: { enabled: true }, red_team: { enabled: true }, research: { enabled: true }, video: { enabled: true }, autonomous_loop: { max_iterations: 5, max_auto_fixes: 10, require_human_approval: true }.

reference_corpus.title: SKILL.md
reference_corpus.text: HackathonOS is an AI Hackathon Mentor/Co-Pilot. Lifecycle has exactly 20 phases. Operations include INIT, CONFIG, CONFIG CHECK, HELP, PHASE, STATUS, NEXT, SUGGEST, IDEA-EVALUATE, PROJECT-PLAN, IMPLEMENT, TESTING-SECURITY, UX-REVIEW, RED-TEAM, JUDGE-SIM, SCORE-OPTIMIZE, DEMO-PREPARE, PRESENTATION-PREPARE, FINAL-AUDIT, SUBMISSION-PREPARE, POSTMORTEM. Master command is /hackathonos. Supported platforms: Claude Code, Kilo Code, OpenCode.

reference_corpus.title: Command manifest
reference_corpus.text: schema_version: 1, master_command: /hackathonos. 29 implemented commands across groups: CORE, CONFIGURATION, INTELLIGENCE, ENGINEERING, PRODUCT QUALITY, FINALIZATION, EMERGENCY. 9 planned commands. Host runtime status: claude NOT VERIFIED, opencode NOT VERIFIED, kilo NOT VERIFIED.

reference_corpus.title: Git ignore
reference_corpus.text: Secrets and local credentials: .env, .env.*, credentials/, credentials.json, secrets/, *.pem, *.key, *.p12, *.pfx, *.jks, id_rsa, service-account.json, secrets.json. AI_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, GOOGLE_API_KEY, GITHUB_TOKEN are secret environment keys.

reference_corpus.title: Command router source
reference_corpus.text: Deterministic command argument routing. Validates manifest schema_version=1, master_command=/hackathonos, resolves routes for status, next, help, init, phase, config, config check, suggest. Checks adapter files for claude, opencode, kilo hosts.

reference_corpus.title: Lifecycle workflow
reference_corpus.text: HackathonOS lifecycle has exactly 20 phases. Phase 1 through Phase 20 are locked sequentially. Each phase has workflow, rules, templates, tests, and audit reports.

reference_corpus.title: Audit reports
reference_corpus.text: Phase audit reports exist for phases 6, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15, 16, 17, 19, 20. Reports verify lifecycle correctness, routing, resource resolution, repository inspection, evidence classification, and quality gates.

reference_corpus.title: Root README
reference_corpus.text: No README.md exists at the repository root. README files exist only in subdirectories (commands/, docs/, adapters/, tests/).

reference_corpus.title: Ideas engine source
reference_corpus.text: Evidence types: FACT, INFERENCE, ASSUMPTION, UNKNOWN. Confidence levels: LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH. Red team levels: KILL, MAJOR CONCERN, MINOR CONCERN. Idea engine validates reports, scores candidates, finds duplicates, and persists immutable run artifacts.
